newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Creditanstalt sale to enter new round next week.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt sale to enter new round next week.

text.p: Austria will enter a fresh round in the marathon sell-off of Creditanstalt next week after a new study on the bank is submitted to the finance minister on Friday, the government said on Thursday.

But the finance ministry insisted no details of the new report would be made public until the offering period for the flagship of the Austrian banking system had been closed, probably some four to six weeks from now.

"We'll get the study tomorrow, but you won't hear anything about it unless you want to make an offer for Creditanstalt and sign a confidentiality agreement first," a spokesman for Finance Minister Viktor Klima said.

Investment house JP Morgan originally submitted a study of the bank a year ago, but Klima asked his advisers to update the report after he turned down the only known bid for the state's 70 percent voting stake in the bank last month.

At current market prices, the government's stake would be worth some 14 billion schillings ($1.3 billion). That is well below the 18 billion figure the finance ministry, eager for new revenue to plug its growing budget holes, had been targeting.
Creditanstalt, the country's number two bank, has topped the government's privatisation list for as long as six years.

A host of suitors has come and gone since the bank was put up for sale in 1990. The most recent bid by Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali was rejected by Klima since the group was reluctant to take on all of the government's 19.9 million ordinary shares in the bank.
-- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274 ($ = 10.82 Austrian Schillings)
